1	# angr-memories — bd memory cleanup archive
2	
3	Snapshot of the three-round cleanup of the `angr` bd memory corpus
4	(2026-06-04 round 1 + 2026-06-05 round 2 + 2026-07-04 round 3). Use this
5	directory to:
6	
7	- Study **what was forgotten** — body archives + per-decision audit logs
8	- Re-run a forgotten memory's recovery — pre-prune snapshots are full JSON dumps
9	- Reuse the **tooling** for future cleanup rounds on this or another bd-backed project
10	- Read back the conversation transcripts that drove the prune decisions
11	
12	This is a frozen mirror of the project's `.bd-prune/` + `.bd-prune-part2/`
13	+ `.bd-prune-part3/` directories plus the live tool scripts at the time of
14	round-3 completion. The original directories remain in the repo (gitignored).
15	
16	## Headline numbers
17	
18	| | Before | After |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| Round 1 (2026-06-04) | 1,296 | 832 (−36%) |
21	| Round 2 (2026-06-05) | 832 | 414 (−50%) |
22	| Round 3 (2026-07-04) | 934 | 757 (−19%) |
23	| Combined           | peak 1,296 | 757 |
24	
25	Round 1 used heuristic triage + light agent review. Round 2 did an
26	exhaustive body-by-body agent review with an aggressive forget/merge
27	posture, plus citation-graph surgery on the residue. Round 3 repeated the
28	round-2 process on the corpus after it regrew from 414 to 934 (four weeks
29	of new work): cheap triage sweeps forgot 70, then an 18-batch exhaustive
30	agent re-review forgot another 70 and merged 66 (37 subordinates folded
31	into 29 canonicals). Zero promotes — the round-2 "when in doubt, forget
32	rather than duplicate docs" precedent held again.
33	
34	## Layout
35	
36	```
37	~/angr-memories/
38	├── README.md            (this file)
39	├── round2-plan.md       (the plan that drove round 2)
40	├── forgotten.txt        — all 1,059 keys removed across 3 rounds, with round/verdict/reason
41	├── survivors.txt        — all 757 surviving keys with first-line preview
42	├── forget_reasons.txt   — reason histogram (495 distinct reasons, sorted by count)
43	├── merges.txt           — 73 merges: subordinate → canonical
44	├── batch_stats.txt      — per-batch verdict counts (all 3 rounds)
45	├── claude-md/
46	│   ├── CLAUDE.md.pre-round2  — state at last git commit (before round 1)
47	│   ├── CLAUDE.md.post-round2 — current state (after both rounds)
48	│   └── CLAUDE.md.diff        — unified diff
49	├── tools/               (the six scripts, post-patch state)
50	│   ├── bd_triage.py             — heuristic tagger; emits triage.csv + cites-graph
51	│   ├── bd_gen_manifest.py       — turns triage tags into a forget manifest
52	│   ├── bd_prune.py              — applies a manifest (forget/merge/promote/keep)
53	│   ├── bd_split_manifest.py     — splits a manifest into -auto + -promote halves
54	│   ├── bd_apply_with_defer.py   — wraps bd_prune.py with auto-defer on orphan errors
55	│   └── bd_chunk_for_review.py   — buckets a snapshot by prefix family for agents
56	├── round1/              (full .bd-prune/ snapshot from 2026-06-04)
57	│   ├── README.md                — round 1 workflow notes
58	│   ├── snapshot-pre-prune.json  — all 1,296 memories at start of round 1
59	│   ├── snapshot-post-prune.json — all 832 memories at end of round 1
60	│   ├── triage.csv               — heuristic tags per key
61	│   ├── cites-graph.json         — {citer: [cited]} citation graph
62	│   ├── manifest-B*.jsonl        — per-batch decisions
63	│   ├── bodies-B*.json           — bodies handed to round-1 agents
64	│   └── decisions.jsonl          — append-only audit log (1226 rows)
65	├── round2/              (full .bd-prune-part2/ snapshot from 2026-06-05)
66	│   ├── batch-index.json         — {batch_id: [keys]} chunking record
67	│   ├── snapshot-pre-prune.json  — all 832 memories at start of round 2
68	│   ├── snapshot-post-prune.json — all 414 memories at end of round 2
69	│   ├── triage.csv               — heuristic tags per key (final state)
70	│   ├── cites-graph.json         — final citation graph
71	│   ├── manifest-R2-*.jsonl      — per-batch decisions
72	│   ├── manifest-R2-*-auto.jsonl — split: forget/merge/keep half
73	│   ├── manifest-R2-*-promote.jsonl       — split: promote half (empty for most batches)
74	│   ├── manifest-R2-*-auto-deferred.jsonl — orphan-deferred rows from auto-apply
75	│   ├── bodies-R2-*.json         — bodies handed to round-2 agents (per batch)
76	│   ├── cites-R2-*.json          — per-batch citation subset given to agents
77	│   ├── decisions.jsonl          — append-only audit log (842 rows)
78	│   └── intermediate/            — temp manifests from the citation-surgery phase
79	│       (orphans retries, promotes-declined, last3 cleanup, etc.)
80	├── round3/              (full .bd-prune-part3/ snapshot from 2026-07-04)
81	│   ├── batch-index.json         — {batch_id: [keys]} chunking record (R3 prefixes)
82	│   ├── snapshot-pre-prune.json  — 864 memories after cheap sweeps, before agent review
83	│   ├── snapshot-pre-prune-original.json — 934 memories at the very start of round 3
84	│   ├── snapshot-post-prune.json — all 757 memories at end of round 3
85	│   ├── triage.csv               — heuristic tags per key (final state)
86	│   ├── cites-graph.json         — final citation graph
87	│   ├── review-instructions.md   — the per-batch agent brief (round-2 decision tree)
88	│   ├── manifest-R3-*.jsonl      — per-batch decisions (18 agent batches + 3 sweeps)
89	│   ├── manifest-R3-*-auto.jsonl — split: forget/merge/keep half
90	│   ├── manifest-R3-*-promote.jsonl — split: promote half (all empty this round)
91	│   ├── manifest-R3-combined-auto.jsonl — all 18 agent batches concatenated for one apply
92	│   ├── bodies-R3-*.json         — bodies handed to round-3 agents (per batch)
93	│   ├── cites-R3-*.json          — per-batch citation subset given to agents
94	│   ├── decisions.jsonl          — append-only audit log (round 3 only)
95	│   └── intermediate/            — citation-surgery originals (2 repaired citers)
96	└── claude-logs/
97	    ├── round1-session.jsonl     — Claude Code transcript driving round 1
98	    ├── round2-session.jsonl     — Claude Code transcript driving round 2
99	    └── round3-session.jsonl     — Claude Code transcript driving round 3
100	```
101	
102	## Common operations
103	
104	### Quick survey of what's gone
105	
106	```bash
107	# Top 20 most-common forget reasons
108	sort forget_reasons.txt | tail -20
109	
110	# Every key forgotten in round 2 with its reason
111	grep '^round2' forgotten.txt | awk -F'\t' '{print $3, $4}'
112	
113	# How aggressive was each batch?
114	cat batch_stats.txt
115	```
116	
117	### List every key forgotten across both rounds
118	
119	```bash
120	jq -r 'select(.verdict=="forget") | .key' round1/decisions.jsonl round2/decisions.jsonl | sort -u
121	# or, with the pre-baked study aid:
122	awk -F'\t' '{print $3}' forgotten.txt | sort -u
123	```
124	
125	### Read a forgotten key's body
126	
127	```bash
128	# Was it forgotten in round 1?
129	python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('round1/snapshot-pre-prune.json')); print(d['<key>'])"
130	
131	# Or round 2? (round-2 pre-prune is the round-1 post-prune state)
132	python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('round2/snapshot-pre-prune.json')); print(d['<key>'])"
133	```
134	
135	### Find what reason was given for forgetting a specific key
136	
137	```bash
138	jq -c 'select(.key=="<key>")' round1/decisions.jsonl round2/decisions.jsonl
139	```
140	
141	### See per-batch agent reasoning
142	
143	The conversation transcripts in `claude-logs/` capture each agent's
144	report (counts, representative forgets, uncertain cases). Each round-2
145	agent invocation produced a ~250-word summary block — search for
146	"R2-INVARIANT-3" etc. in `round2-session.jsonl`.
147	
148	```bash
149	# Show only the assistant turns from the round-2 session
150	python3 -c "
151	import json
152	for ln in open('claude-logs/round2-session.jsonl'):
153	    r = json.loads(ln)
154	    if r.get('type') == 'assistant' and r.get('message', {}).get('content'):
155	        for c in r['message']['content']:
156	            if c.get('type') == 'text':
157	                print(c['text']); print('---')
158	" | less
159	```
160	
161	### Reuse the tools on another bd-backed project
162	
163	The six scripts in `tools/` are self-contained. To kick off a cleanup:
164	
165	```bash
166	cd <your-project>
167	mkdir -p .bd-prune
168	bd memories --json > .bd-prune/snapshot-pre-prune.json
169	python3 /path/to/tools/bd_triage.py --prune-dir .bd-prune
170	python3 /path/to/tools/bd_chunk_for_review.py --prune-dir .bd-prune
171	# then per-batch: spawn an agent, write manifest, then:
172	python3 /path/to/tools/bd_split_manifest.py .bd-prune/manifest-X.jsonl
173	python3 /path/to/tools/bd_apply_with_defer.py .bd-prune/manifest-X-auto.jsonl --prune-dir .bd-prune
174	```
175	
176	The mandatory keep-list (`DEFAULT_KEEP_LIST` in `bd_gen_manifest.py`)
177	is angr-specific — replace with your project's anchors before reuse.
178	
179	## Round-2 highlights worth re-reading
180	
181	- **Aggressive prompt design** (round1 vs round2 INV-1): the first
182	  INV-1 attempt with mild prompting produced 2 forgets out of 65; the
183	  re-run with explicit "the bar for keep is X" framing produced 18
184	  forgets + 4 merges. See `claude-logs/round2-session.jsonl` for the
185	  diff.
186	- **Cited-by guard fixed-point bug**: round-1's `bd_gen_manifest.py`
187	  did one pass and missed a chain orphan
188	  (`avoid-dfs-coupling-for-shared-lineage`). Round 2 fixed this — see
189	  the patch in `tools/bd_gen_manifest.py` `while True` block.
190	- **Citation surgery on mandatory keeps**: three CLAUDE.md anchors had
191	  "see also X" refs to stale targets. Surgery let the targets go
192	  without losing anchor content. Search the round-2 log for
193	  "benchmark-bimodal-variance-rules" or "iop-avg-vs-hadd-distinction".
194	- **Promote candidates declined**: rust_engine.rst already covered the
195	  state.inspect supported-event matrix and SimOption raise list; INV-3
196	  agent's promotes were rejected. Useful precedent for "when in doubt,
197	  forget rather than duplicate".
198	
199	## Round-3 notes worth re-reading
200	
201	- **Full re-review at scale**: unlike a delta-only pass, round 3 re-judged
202	  all 864 post-sweep memories (including the 414 round-2 survivors) across
203	  18 prefix-family batches. Net result was gentler (−19%) than round 2
204	  because the round-2 survivors were already scrubbed — most round-3 forgets
205	  came from the ~520 keys added in the intervening four weeks (iteration
206	  receipts, clippy-progress snapshots, completed-refactor commit scraps).
207	- **One combined apply, not batch-by-batch**: all 18 agent manifests were
208	  concatenated into `manifest-R3-combined-auto.jsonl` and applied once via
209	  `bd_apply_with_defer.py`. A combined apply gives the most accurate
210	  cited-by guard — a forget is only blocked if a *surviving* memory cites
211	  it, whereas per-batch applies would falsely defer a key cited only by
212	  another to-be-forgotten memory in a later batch.
213	- **Citation surgery (2 keys)**: `djq7-evidence-needs-file-io-harness` and
214	  `xmllint-vanilla-symex-probe` were each cited only by the memory that
215	  superseded them (a "supersedes X" / "refutes X" prose back-reference).
216	  The two citers were rephrased to drop the dangling name before forgetting;
217	  originals archived in `round3/intermediate/`.
218	- **Zero promotes again**: no memory cleared the ≥800-char durable-and-not-
219	  already-in-docs bar. Same precedent as round 2.
220	- **Tooling change**: `bd_chunk_for_review.py` gained a `--round` flag
221	  (defaults to `R2` for backcompat) so batch IDs/filenames aren't hardcoded
222	  to one round.
223	
224	## Recovery
225	
226	If a forgotten key turns out to be load-bearing:
227	
228	```bash
229	python3 -c "
230	import json, subprocess
231	# Try newest snapshot first (each round's pre-prune == prior round's post-prune,
232	# modulo corpus regrowth between rounds)
233	for snap in ('round3/snapshot-pre-prune-original.json',
234	             'round2/snapshot-pre-prune.json', 'round1/snapshot-pre-prune.json'):
235	    d = json.load(open(snap))
236	    if '<key>' in d:
237	        body = d['<key>']
238	        subprocess.run(['bd','remember', body, '--key', '<key>'], check=True)
239	        print(f'restored from {snap}')
240	        break
241	else:
242	    raise SystemExit('not found')
243	"
244	```
245

## Round-2 highlights worth re-reading

- **Aggressive prompt design** (round1 vs round2 INV-1): the first
  INV-1 attempt with mild prompting produced 2 forgets out of 65; the
  re-run with explicit "the bar for keep is X" framing produced 18
  forgets + 4 merges. See `claude-logs/round2-session.jsonl` for the
  diff.
- **Cited-by guard fixed-point bug**: round-1's `bd_gen_manifest.py`
  did one pass and missed a chain orphan
  (`avoid-dfs-coupling-for-shared-lineage`). Round 2 fixed this — see
  the patch in `tools/bd_gen_manifest.py` `while True` block.
- **Citation surgery on mandatory keeps**: three CLAUDE.md anchors had
  "see also X" refs to stale targets. Surgery let the targets go
  without losing anchor content. Search the round-2 log for
  "benchmark-bimodal-variance-rules" or "iop-avg-vs-hadd-distinction".
- **Promote candidates declined**: rust_engine.rst already covered the
  state.inspect supported-event matrix and SimOption raise list; INV-3
  agent's promotes were rejected. Useful precedent for "when in doubt,
  forget rather than duplicate".

## Round-3 notes worth re-reading

- **Full re-review at scale**: unlike a delta-only pass, round 3 re-judged
  all 864 post-sweep memories (including the 414 round-2 survivors) across
  18 prefix-family batches. Net result was gentler (−19%) than round 2
  because the round-2 survivors were already scrubbed — most round-3 forgets
  came from the ~520 keys added in the intervening four weeks (iteration
  receipts, clippy-progress snapshots, completed-refactor commit scraps).
- **One combined apply, not batch-by-batch**: all 18 agent manifests were
  concatenated into `manifest-R3-combined-auto.jsonl` and applied once via
  `bd_apply_with_defer.py`. A combined apply gives the most accurate
  cited-by guard — a forget is only blocked if a *surviving* memory cites
  it, whereas per-batch applies would falsely defer a key cited only by
  another to-be-forgotten memory in a later batch.
- **Citation surgery (2 keys)**: `djq7-evidence-needs-file-io-harness` and
  `xmllint-vanilla-symex-probe` were each cited only by the memory that
  superseded them (a "supersedes X" / "refutes X" prose back-reference).
  The two citers were rephrased to drop the dangling name before forgetting;
  originals archived in `round3/intermediate/`.
- **Zero promotes again**: no memory cleared the ≥800-char durable-and-not-
  already-in-docs bar. Same precedent as round 2.
- **Tooling change**: `bd_chunk_for_review.py` gained a `--round` flag
  (defaults to `R2` for backcompat) so batch IDs/filenames aren't hardcoded
  to one round.

```bash
python3 -c "
import json, subprocess
# Try newest snapshot first (each round's pre-prune == prior round's post-prune,
# modulo corpus regrowth between rounds)
for snap in ('round3/snapshot-pre-prune-original.json',
             'round2/snapshot-pre-prune.json', 'round1/snapshot-pre-prune.json'):
    d = json.load(open(snap))
    if '<key>' in d:
        body = d['<key>']
        subprocess.run(['bd','remember', body, '--key', '<key>'], check=True)
        print(f'restored from {snap}')
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit('not found')
"
```

    ap.add_argument("--exclude-cluster", default=None,
                    help="comma list of prefixes to exclude")
    ap.add_argument("--max-cluster", type=int, default=None,

    ap.add_argument("--keep-list", default=",".join(sorted(DEFAULT_KEEP_LIST)))
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    triage_csv = args.prune_dir / "triage.csv"
    cites_json = args.prune_dir / "cites-graph.json"

    keep_set = set(args.keep_list.split(","))
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(triage_csv.open()))
    live = _live_memories()
    cites_graph = json.loads(cites_json.read_text()) if cites_json.exists() else {}

    selected: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for r in rows:
        key = r["key"]
        if key not in live:
            continue
        if key in keep_set:
            continue
        if args.closed_only and r["closed_only"] != "1":

        if args.no_bead and r["no_bead"] != "1":

        if args.reference_type and r["reference_type"] != "1":

        if args.future_date and r["future_date"] != "1":
            continue
        if args.prefix and r["prefix"] != args.prefix:
            continue
        if args.prefix_in:
            if r["prefix"] not in args.prefix_in.split(","):
                continue
        if args.exclude_cluster:
            if r["prefix"] in args.exclude_cluster.split(","):
                continue
        if args.min_cluster is not None and int(r["cluster_size"]) < args.min_cluster:
            continue
        if args.max_cluster is not None and int(r["cluster_size"]) > args.max_cluster:
            continue
        selected.append(r)

    # Cited-by guard: forgetting key X is unsafe if any LIVE memory we're
    # NOT forgetting cites X. Iterate to fixed point — when a deferral
    # turns a "soon-to-be-forgotten" citer into a "surviving" citer, its
    # cite targets need a fresh check.
    to_forget = {r["key"] for r in selected}
    all_blocked: set[str] = set()
    while True:
        surviving_citers = {
            citer: cited for citer, cited in cites_graph.items()
            if citer in live and citer not in to_forget
        }

cd ~/repos/angr-memories && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

R4 = Path('round4')
pre = json.load(open(R4/'snapshot-pre-prune-original.json'))
post = json.load(open(R4/'snapshot-post-prune.json'))

# collect round-4 decisions: sweep manifest + combined manifest
rows = []
for mf in ['manifest-R4-status.jsonl', 'manifest-R4-combined-auto.jsonl']:
    rows += [json.loads(l) for l in open(R4/mf)]

gone = set(pre) - set(post)
by_key = {r['key']: r for r in rows}

# forgotten.txt: append round4 rows (forgets + merge subordinates)
with open('forgotten.txt','a') as f:
    for k in sorted(gone):
        r = by_key.get(k, {})
        verdict = r.get('verdict','forget')
        if verdict == 'merge' and not r.get('canonical'):
            verdict = 'merge-subordinate'
        reason = r.get('reason','(status sweep)').replace('\t',' ').replace('\n',' ')
        f.write(f"round4\t{verdict}\t{k}\t{reason}\n")

# merges.txt: append round4 subordinate -> canonical
with open('merges.txt','a') as f:
    for r in rows:
        if r.get('verdict')=='merge' and not r.get('canonical'):
            reason = r.get('reason','').replace('\n',' ')
            f.write(f"{r['key']} -> {r['merged_into']}  [round4] {reason}\n")

# survivors.txt: regenerate from post snapshot
with open('survivors.txt','w') as f:
    f.write(f"# Keys that survived all four rounds ({len(post)} memories)\n\n")
    for k in sorted(post):
        first = post[k].replace('\n',' ')[:120]
        f.write(f"{k}\t{first}\n")

# batch_stats.txt: append round4 per-batch counts
stats = {}
for r in rows:
    b = r.get('batch','R4-?')
    stats.setdefault(b, Counter())[r['verdict']] += 1
with open('batch_stats.txt','a') as f:
    f.write('\n# --- round 4 (2026-07-20) ---\n')
    for b in sorted(stats):
        c = stats[b]
        tot = sum(c.values())
        f.write(f"  {b:32}{c['forget']:6}{c['merge']:8}{c['promote']:9}{c['keep']:8}{tot:8}\n")

# forget_reasons.txt: regenerate histogram from forgotten.txt
reasons = Counter()
for ln in open('forgotten.txt'):
    if ln.startswith('#') or not ln.strip(): continue
    parts = ln.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
    if len(parts) >= 4:
        reasons[parts[3]] += 1
with open('forget_reasons.txt','w') as f:
    f.write('# Forget-reason histogram (top reasons by frequency)\n\n')
    for reason, n in reasons.most_common():
        f.write(f"{n:5}  {reason}\n")

print('forgotten appended:', len(gone))
print('survivors written:', len(post))
print('round4 batches:', len(stats))
EOF
